clue.text: Something from saint regarding life in church, primarily

parts.note: re is the short Latin-derived word for 'regarding' or 'concerning'

indicators.note: primarily means firstly, so only the opening letter of each of these three words is used

explanation.surface: A sacred object linked to a saint, said to concern life in the church at its most basic.
explanation.definitionFit: A holy relic is a bone or possession kept as a memento of a saint.

clue.text: Extremes of raffish yet humdrum beat

indicators.note: the extremes of a word are its first and last letters, taken here from each of the three words

explanation.surface: A dull rhythm that is also rakish, at its edges.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Extremes of' takes RH, YT and HM.
explanation.definitionFit: A beat in music is its pulse or regular rhythm; close synonym.

clue.text: Lake to merit study

parts.note: L is the map abbreviation for lake
to merit something is to earn it

explanation.surface: A lake deserving to be examined.
explanation.definitionFit: To study is to acquire knowledge; to learn is the same, a verb synonym.

clue.text: French city embracing southern region covered by emperor

indicators.note: embracing means holding around, so the city surrounds the other pieces

parts.note: Caen is a city in Normandy
an area is a region

explanation.surface: A French town takes in a southern area ruled by an emperor.
explanation.definitionFit: Caesarean means relating to a Caesar, an emperor, so territory under his rule is described thus.

clue.text: Wandering, taking colt for run — very nice

indicators.note: taking one thing for another signals that a letter is swapped in place of the other
for marks what is being replaced: the colt goes in where the run was

parts.note: a wandering mind is delirious, rambling in fever
R is the cricket scoring abbreviation for run
C stands for colt in racing form guides

explanation.surface: Someone rambling, accepting a young horse instead of a run, finds it very nice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking colt for run' puts C where R was in DELIRIOUS.
explanation.definitionFit: Something delicious is extremely pleasant, especially to the taste; a synonym of very nice.

clue.text: What's less common in the German geriatric?

indicators.note: in signals that one word goes inside the other

parts.note: der is the German masculine word for the
odder means stranger or more unusual

explanation.surface: A question about what is rarer in the elderly German.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What's' is only a link; 'geriatric' is used as a noun for an old person.
explanation.definitionFit: A dodderer is a shaky, feeble old person; geriatric used as a noun for an aged person.

clue.text: Smoothly set up a big tent without power

indicators.note: in a down entry up means the letters read upwards, reversed

parts.note: to gel is to set, like a jelly

indicators.note: without means lacking, so the letter is removed

parts.note: the big top is the circus tent; here the clue takes TOP for it
P is the physics symbol for power

explanation.surface: Erecting a large marquee calmly, with no electricity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns GEL into LEG; 'without' strips P from TOP, the circus big top, leaving TO.
explanation.definitionFit: Legato is a musical direction meaning play smoothly, notes joined without breaks.

clue.text: Making point on being imprisoned by military leader

indicators.note: imprisoned by means held inside, so the short word goes within the leader

parts.note: CIC stands for commander-in-chief

explanation.surface: Making a case while locked up by a general.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Making point' is the definition: think of a shape that tapers to a tip, not an argument.
explanation.definitionFit: Conic means cone-shaped, a shape tapering to a point.

clue.text: Part of hospital engaged in determinedly removing stones to all appearances

indicators.note: engaged in means placed within, so the hospital part sits inside
removing signals that letters are taken out

parts.note: stoutly means resolutely or determinedly
ST is the abbreviation for stone, the British weight unit
a ward is a room or section of a hospital

explanation.surface: A hospital ward busy taking out kidney stones with determination.
explanation.walkthrough: The stone is a British weight of 14 pounds; 'removing' leaves OUTLY, and 'engaged in' puts the ward within it.
explanation.definitionFit: Outwardly means as far as can be seen on the surface; an idiom of the same sense.

clue.text: Element in southern building Queen fails to open

indicators.note: fails to open means the opening letters are missing

parts.note: an erection is a building
ER stands for Elizabeth Regina, the Queen

explanation.surface: Part of a southern structure that the Queen did not inaugurate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fails to open' drops ER from the start of ERECTION.
explanation.definitionFit: A section is a component or element of a larger whole; synonym.

clue.text: Books prepared now? Certainly make an opening for that

parts.note: yea is an old word of assent, meaning yes or certainly
to rend is to tear, which makes an opening

explanation.surface: Accounts are ready now; surely that justifies creating a gap.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic: the books (accounts) are made ready at the close of the financial year.
explanation.definitionFit: Accounts are closed and prepared at the end of the financial year, so the question mark points to that time.

clue.text: Information to quote back describing family links

parts.note: gen is British slang for information

indicators.note: back tells us to write the word for quoting backwards

parts.note: to cite is to quote a source

explanation.surface: Data to be repeated, describing family connections.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gen' is British slang for information.
explanation.definitionFit: Genetic traits are inherited, so the word describes links passed down through families.

clue.text: Afghan let rebels move to the right? On the contrary

definitions.text: move to the right? On the contrary

indicators.note: rebels as a verb means rises up and breaks ranks, so the letters break out of order

explanation.surface: An Afghan permits insurgents to shift rightwards, or rather the opposite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'rebels' rearranges AFGHANLET. The definition reverses 'move to the right' with 'On the contrary', giving a move to the left.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means to turn left, the contrary of moving to the right.

clue.text: Pelt one carnivore

parts.note: an animal's pelt is its coat of fur
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: The skin of a single meat-eater.
explanation.definitionFit: The coati is a South American raccoon relative, classed among the carnivores.

clue.text: Religious follower: inner nature's not Catholic

indicators.note: not here means without, so the Catholic letter is dropped

parts.note: essence is a thing's inner nature; the 's stands for 'is'

explanation.surface: A believer whose inner nature is not Catholic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not' removes C from ESSENCE.
explanation.definitionFit: The Essenes were an ascetic Jewish sect, so a member was a follower of a religion.

clue.text: Give a better view of dreadful court saga

indicators.note: dreadful suggests something badly wrecked, so the letters come out jumbled

explanation.surface: Present a terrible legal drama in a kinder light.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dreadful' rearranges COURT SAGA.
explanation.definitionFit: To sugar-coat something is to make it seem more palatable than it is; an idiom.

clue.text: Excellent Government of previous years

parts.note: olden means of former times, as in olden days

explanation.surface: Praise for a past administration.
explanation.definitionFit: A golden opportunity or performance is a superb one; figurative sense of the precious metal.

clue.text: Blocks former schoolfellow taking pompous moves about college

parts.note: OB is an old boy, a former pupil of a school

indicators.note: about means around, so the walks surround the college letter

parts.note: struts are swaggering, self-important walks

explanation.surface: A former classmate swaggers round a college and gets in the way.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts C inside STRUTS.
explanation.definitionFit: To obstruct is to block, hinder or get in the way; verb synonym.

clue.text: Staff travelled endlessly

indicators.note: endlessly means without its end, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: rode is past tense of ride, so travelled on horse or vehicle

explanation.surface: Employees who commuted without stopping.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts the last letter from RODE.
explanation.definitionFit: A rod is a stick or staff, such as a stick carried as a symbol of office.

clue.text: Mad cat lady's right regarding feet

indicators.note: mad means crazy, so the letters go wild

explanation.surface: An eccentric woman with many cats is correct about feet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mad' rearranges CAT LADY to DACTYLA; the 's is a link. Feet here are metrical units.
explanation.definitionFit: Dactylar relates to dactyls, metrical feet of one long and two short syllables.

clue.text: Cricket side to terminate famous player?

parts.note: the leg side is one half of a cricket field, the half behind the batter's legs
to end is to terminate

explanation.surface: A cricket team finishing off a well-known player.
explanation.walkthrough: In cricket the leg side is the half of the field on the batter's leg side, the other being the off side.
explanation.definitionFit: A sporting legend is a renowned player, an informal sense of the word.

clue.text: Vessel relieved of some cargo?

definitions.meaning: a flat-bottomed barge used to unload ships
with some load taken off, so less heavy

explanation.surface: A boat with part of its freight taken off.
explanation.definitionFit: A lighter is a barge that lightens ships, and the comparative of light means less heavy.

clue.text: Tests for one importing dope? On the contrary

indicators.note: importing means taking in, so one piece goes inside the other
On the contrary swaps the roles: the dope takes in the example rather than the reverse

parts.note: a dope is a fool, an ass
for one means for example, as does say

explanation.surface: Checks on a person who brings in drugs.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads as SAY importing ASS; 'On the contrary' flips it so ASS takes in SAY: AS(SAY)S.
explanation.definitionFit: Assays are chemical analyses that test metals or substances for purity.

clue.text: Better cut the off-the-cuff humour

indicators.note: cut means shortened, so the final letter goes

parts.note: to better is to improve

explanation.surface: Spontaneous comedy is better trimmed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cut' drops the last letter of IMPROVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Improv is improvised comedy made up on the spot, without a script.

clue.text: Make fun of aspiration when in drink

indicators.note: when in places one piece inside another

parts.note: to sup is to drink
an end is an aim or aspiration

explanation.surface: Mocking someone's ambitions while drunk.
explanation.walkthrough: 'aspiration' looks like breath or hope, but it gives a goal: an end.
explanation.definitionFit: To send up is British for mocking or parodying someone; an idiom.

clue.text: Young ladies from both sides embraced by US soldiers

indicators.note: embraced by means held inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: GIs are American enlisted soldiers
right and left are both sides, abbreviated R and L

explanation.surface: Young women from either side are hugged by American troops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'both sides' gives right and left, abbreviated.
explanation.definitionFit: Girls are female children or young women; synonym of young ladies.

clue.text: Greeting given to South American and Asian food

indicators.note: given to means added after the other pieces

parts.note: US means American
hi is a greeting

explanation.surface: A hello offered to a South American and to some Asian food.
explanation.definitionFit: Sushi is a Japanese dish of vinegared rice with raw fish.

clue.text: Transport I broke up after test of roadworthiness

indicators.note: after says the rearranged letters follow the test

parts.note: the MOT is the annual British vehicle safety test

indicators.note: up as in broken up, so the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: A vehicle I damaged after its safety inspection.
explanation.walkthrough: The MOT is the annual British roadworthiness test for vehicles; 'up' mixes I BROKE, placed 'after' it.
explanation.definitionFit: A motorbike is a means of transport, an example of a vehicle.

clue.text: Set deep in main terminal

indicators.note: in signals that the answer lies within the letters of these words

explanation.surface: Something set deep in the main terminal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' points to letters within mAIN TERminal.
explanation.definitionFit: To inter is to bury, placing something deep in the ground.

clue.text: Pocket, or most of possible container thereof

indicators.note: most of means all but the final letter

parts.note: trousers have pockets, so they may contain one

explanation.surface: A pouch, or most of the garment that might hold it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'most of' drops the last letter of TROUSERS. Pocket is a verb here.
explanation.definitionFit: To trouser money is British slang for pocketing it, taking it for oneself.

clue.text: Found officer retreating at the last, having lost heart

indicators.note: retreating means going backwards, so the officer's letters reverse

parts.note: Col is short for colonel, an army officer

indicators.note: having lost heart means the middle letter goes

parts.note: the last is the end

explanation.surface: A soldier turned up retreating in the end, discouraged.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retreating' turns COL into LOC; 'having lost heart' takes the middle from END, leaving ED.
explanation.definitionFit: Found and located both mean discovered where something is; past tense synonyms.

clue.text: Dog further tested, mostly excessively, having tail docked

indicators.note: mostly means all but the last letter

parts.note: retried means tried or tested again

indicators.note: a docked tail is cut short, so the final letter goes

parts.note: very can mean exceedingly or excessively

explanation.surface: A dog tested again, too severely, ended up with its tail cut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' takes RETRIE from RETRIED; 'having tail docked' cuts VERY to VER.
explanation.definitionFit: A retriever is a gundog breed, such as the Labrador or golden retriever.

clue.text: Sweet stuff in second year concluded

parts.note: up means finished, as in time is up

explanation.surface: A treat finished in the second year.
explanation.definitionFit: Syrup is a thick sugary liquid, a kind of sweet stuff.
